title: The Search Box
primary_metric: estimated probability of detection (POD) per flight-hour, for each candidate search box

options.A: The Windward Datum -- send the helicopter to the search box generated by the wind-driven leeway drift model
options.B: The Set-and-Drift Datum -- send the helicopter to the search box generated by the current-driven drift model

cohort_bands.note: Run the D1-D3 conversion/parametric/elimination steps as a full-group walkthrough before splitting into pairs for D4/D5; a room this size does not reliably self-sort into a Windward-vs-Set-and-Drift split at Anchor 1's vote, so call on individuals by name during Anchor 2-4 rather than relying on volunteers.

The Anchor 1 vote should produce a real, visible split; use it. Pair students across the split for the Data Deep Dive so each pair has to defend both D5 numbers to a partner who initially disagreed, and give the Twist its full 5 minutes (15:00-20:00) before recommitting -- a room this size needs the extra beat to actually re-run the growth-rate math, not just re-vote on gut feel.

Break into 4-5 small groups for D1-D4 so every student does the parametric-to-polar chain themselves rather than watching one pair work it at the board; reconvene for D5 and the vote/Twist/recommit sequence as a full room. At this size, cold-calling for the Data Deep Dive (as written) needs a seating chart or name-draw, not open volunteering, or the same 3-4 voices will carry the room.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA13 (Windward Datum's assumed probability of containment, 55%) is not a published figure -- CGADD Figure H-22 shows the real, physically-knowable divergent-datum POC curve sitting below the single-point-datum curve, but only as a graph with no companion numeric table, so no exact digit could be read to a defensible precision. 55% is a documented good-faith estimate below Option B's real, sourced 64.75% single-point POC (S8), consistent with the graph's qualitative shape. sensitivity_model.py (2026-08-31, Tier 2 Probe 5) confirms this dial flips the recommendation at a +50% swing (55% to 82.5%) and breaks the SPEC Sec2 20% cap in both directions, with a real flip threshold of approximately 64.75% (Option A's POC crossing Option B's sourced figure), not the ~61% originally estimated in case.md's Appendix F prose. See FACILITATOR.md's Balance flag section for the full verified numbers.

sources.claim: Reference helicopter search speed for a Person-in-Water pattern (speed-correction factor = 1.0)
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Table H-9 "Search Aircraft Speed Correction"
sources.note: 90 kt is the helicopter reference speed for a Person in Water target (correction factor 1.0 in the table); other speeds (60/120/140 kt) carry non-unity correction factors.

sources.claim: Uncorrected visual sweep width for a Person in Water wearing a PFD, helicopter search, 300 ft altitude, 5 NM visibility
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Table H-15 "Uncorrected Visual Sweep Width – Helicopters for Altitudes 300–500 Feet" and its PFD footnote
sources.note: Base table value for Person in Water at 300 ft/5 NM visibility is 0.1 NM; the table's own footnote multiplies this by 4 for a person known to be wearing a PFD, giving 0.4 NM. Track spacing (P06) is derived from this sweep width at a baseline coverage factor of 1.0 (S = W).

sources.claim: PIW ("Vertical") leeway-speed equation, divergence angle, and leeway-speed standard error
sources.value: Leeway (kts) = 0.011 x Wind (kts) + 0.07 kts; divergence +/-30 deg; standard error 0.35 kt
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Table H-7 "Leeway Speed and Direction Values for Drift Objects" (compiled from Allen & Plourde, 1999)
sources.note: PIW "Vertical" is the closest published category to a person kept upright in the water by a flotation device (as opposed to Sitting/Survival Suit/Scuba Suit/Deceased sub-categories). Table H-7 gives leeway speed as a linear equation of wind speed, not a pure percentage; the slope term (0.011) is ~1.1% of wind speed.

sources.claim: Coverage-factor formulas: C = Sweep Width / Track Spacing, and C = (Sweep Width x Search Speed x Search Endurance) / Area
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Section H.5.5 "Coverage Factor (C)"
sources.note: Formula, not a single value; used in Appendix E and in the FACILITATOR-only margin computation.

sources.claim: Probability-of-detection formula for Normal Search Conditions: POD = 1 - e^(-C)
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Section H.5.6.2(c) and Figure H-21 "Maritime Probability of Detection"
sources.note: Closed-form equation given explicitly in the source for coverage values beyond the graphed range (>3.0); used identically for both options.

sources.claim: Search endurance = 85% of on-scene endurance (remaining 15% reserved for identifying sighted objects and end-of-leg turns)
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Section H.5.2.2
sources.note: Applied to the stated on-scene-endurance-remaining scenario assumption (MA3) to derive the 3.8-hour search endurance figure.

sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Table 5-3 "Coast Guard Aircraft Characteristics"
sources.note: Used only as the real-world ceiling informing the scenario's assumed remaining on-scene endurance (MA3); the specific fuel state at the decision point is scenario-specific and not itself published.

sources.claim: Probability of containment produced by an optimal search factor of 1.1, single-point datum, prior to any searching
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Section H.5.6.3(a)(1) and Figure H-24 "Manual Solution for Square Search Area"
sources.note: Used directly as Option B's POC, since Option B (current-driven) has no stated divergence angle and is therefore modeled as a single-point datum.

sources.claim: Divergent-datum POC curves sit below the single-point-datum curve at a given search factor (graph only, no companion table of exact values)
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Figure H-22 "Probability of Containment (POC) For Single Point and Divergent Datums"
sources.note: Grounds only the qualitative direction of MA13 (Option A's POC assumption is below Option B's real 64.75%); the source gives no exact tabulated digit for the divergent-datum curves at a given search factor, so the specific 55% value is a stated Modeling Assumption, not read off this figure.

sources.claim: Total probable error of position (E) as the 50%-containment radius; search radius = optimal search factor (fs) x E
sources.title: The U.S. Coast Guard Addendum to the United States National Search and Rescue Supplement (NSS) to the IAMSAR, COMDTINST M16130.2F, Sections H.2.1.1 and H.5.6.3
sources.note: Applied identically to both options (search radius R = 1.1 x E(t)), with E(t) driven by each option's own drift-uncertainty growth rate (Appendices C and D).

deliverables.text: A rectangular-datum conversion: convert the vessel's last-known radar fix, given as a polar coordinate (bearing and range from the vessel), into rectangular coordinates on this case's search grid.

Two parametric drift models: for the wind-driven leeway model and the current-driven model, write the person's position as parametric equations x(t) and y(t) in terms of elapsed time since the last fix.

Two eliminated-parameter search boxes: for each drift model, eliminate the time parameter from D2's equations to obtain a rectangular equation for that model's drift centerline, and use it to state the corner coordinates of a rectangular search box.
A graphed polar boundary for each option: graph the polar equation r(θ) describing the outer boundary of each candidate box's search radius around its drifted datum.
A probability-of-detection decision table: for each option, the area enclosed by its D3/D4 search box, available flight-hours, and an estimated POD per flight-hour, with a stated recommendation.

appendices.title: Wind-Driven Leeway Drift Model Data (Option A)

balance.argument_a: The Windward Datum is anchored to real, published leeway coefficients specific to the object category in the water: a sourced equation (Leeway = 0.011 x Wind Speed + 0.07 kt) with a stated +/-30-degree divergence angle (S3), applied here to a 20-knot on-scene wind (MA8) to give a leeway speed of 0.29 kt and a resulting 3.706-sq-NM search box -- the SMALLER of the two candidate boxes, fully searchable at a coverage factor near 37 (versus Option B's roughly 22) inside the helicopter's stated 3.8-hour endurance. A model built from decades of controlled drift-buoy studies specific to this exact object category is a defensible basis for a time-critical recommendation, even before Appendix E's probability-of-containment figures are weighed.
balance.argument_b: The Set-and-Drift Datum tracks the same elapsed 2.5 hours (MA2) and the same converted radar fix, but follows a 1.3-knot on-scene surface current (MA10) instead of wind -- current can dominate leeway when an object rides lower in the water or when current speed is high relative to wind, and unlike the Windward Datum, the Set-and-Drift Datum carries no stated divergence angle, so it is modeled as a single-point datum with a real, sourced 64.75% probability of containment (S8) rather than a discounted, unsourced one. Even though its 6.126-sq-NM box is larger than Option A's, both options remain coverage-saturated (POD near 100% for each) at the stated 90-knot search speed and 0.4-NM sweep width, so Option B's roughly 18% higher containment probability translates directly into a higher estimated detection rate per flight-hour.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendices A-E are sourced or stated as Modeling Assumptions, margin_pct compares the two boxes' estimated probability of detection per flight-hour: (POD_A/flight-hour) vs (POD_B/flight-hour), each computed from that option's D3/D4 search-box area, Appendix A's available flight-hours, and Appendix E's probability-of-containment and coverage-factor data. Recorded as null until case-research fills those figures.

computed_2026-08-30.note: Both options are coverage-saturated (POD ~= 100%) given the stated helicopter endurance/sweep width relative to either box's area, so the margin is driven almost entirely by the POC gap (Appendix E) -- i.e. by MA13 (Option A's assumed divergent-datum POC discount) and, more weakly, by MA12 (Option B's assumed current-model search-radius growth rate). This matches the case's own stated 'trap' in FACILITATOR.md: box size/POD alone does not decide it, POC does.

sensitivity_check_2026-08-31.note: Verified 2026-08-31 against sensitivity_model.py, Tier 2 Probe 5. Corrects case.md's original Appendix F prose (which claimed MA12 flips the recommendation below ~0.35 kt and MA13 flips it above ~61%) -- see FACILITATOR.md's Balance flag section for the full writeup.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Elapsed time, person-overboard report to last radar fix
modeling_assumptions.basis: Narrative color only; does not enter the drift math.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None -- does not affect either box or the recommendation.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Elapsed time, last radar fix to decision point (t in D2's parametric equations)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Representative real SAR response timeline (muster, launch, transit) before a helicopter can be committed to a box.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales both boxes' drift distance and search-radius growth by the same factor -- does not by itself favor one option, but a much shorter/longer time changes both magnitudes together.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Helicopter on-scene endurance remaining, before the real 85% search-efficiency rule is applied
modeling_assumptions.basis: Informed by the real H-60 MAX endurance of 6.0 hours (S7); assumes ~1.5 hours already used for standby/transit.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Raises/lowers the coverage factor equally for both options -- does not by itself favor one option, but a much smaller value could pull both options out of POD saturation and make the recommendation depend on box area again.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Visibility used to read the real sweep-width table (S2)
modeling_assumptions.basis: Plausible daytime, non-adverse visibility, chosen to select a real table column rather than invent a sweep-width number.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Same sweep width applies to both options -- does not favor one over the other.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Arbitrary scenario placement, needed only so D1 has a concrete point to convert from.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None -- translates both derived datums identically.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Radar bearing from vessel to person in the water
modeling_assumptions.basis: Scenario-only; needed as the polar angle for D1's conversion.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Radar range from vessel to person in the water
modeling_assumptions.basis: Scenario-only, short range consistent with a small, low-radar-cross-section target.
Scenario-only, moderate breeze plausible for an open-water SAR case.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Feeds the real leeway-speed equation (S3), changing Option A's drift distance/location, not box size or POD -- does not affect the recommendation on its own.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen to differ from the current direction (MA11) so the two boxes visibly diverge, per the case narrative.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes box location, not size/POD -- does not affect the recommendation on its own.
Feeds Option B's drift distance (location) only.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Chosen to diverge from the wind direction (MA9).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Changes box location, not size/POD -- does not affect the recommendation on its own.

modeling_assumptions.basis: NOT FOUND as a published figure -- no per-hour surface-current standard-error table analogous to Table H-7's leeway standard error was found in the CGADD or reviewed NOAA/USCG SAR literature; set to the same order of magnitude as the real 0.35-kt/hr wind-model figure (S3) for comparability.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Can flip the recommendation. Main driver of Option B's box area (Area_B ~ growth-rate^2); since both options are currently POD-saturated, this interacts with MA13 to set the margin. A future real figure smaller than ~0.35 kt narrows Option B's advantage and could flip the recommendation.

modeling_assumptions.basis: CGADD Figure H-22 (S9) shows divergent-datum POC curves visibly below the single-point-datum curve (Option A has a real, sourced +/-30 deg divergence angle, S3), but the source gives only a graph with no companion numeric table, so no exact digit could be read to a defensible precision.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Can flip the recommendation -- the single largest lever in the current ~15% margin. Raising Option A's assumed POC above roughly 61% (holding Option B's real 64.75% and both near-saturated PODs fixed) flips the recommendation to Option A.
